scholarships.title: New Zealand Refugee Health Scholarship
scholarships.degree: Bachelor's, Master's, Postgraduate Certificate, Postgraduate Diploma, Graduate Certificate, Graduate Diploma
scholarships.official_source: Immigration New Zealand (Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment)

eligibility: Be a former refugee or the child of a refugee
Have resettled in New Zealand through the UNHCR Quota Programme, the Convention Refugee pathway, or the Community Organisation Refugee Sponsorship Category
Be studying or intending to study a health-related qualification in New Zealand
existing.eligibility_summary: Open to former refugees and the children of refugees who resettled in New Zealand through the UNHCR Quota Programme, the Convention Refugee pathway, or the Community Organisation Refugee Sponsorship Category, who are studying a health-related qualification in New Zealand.
benefits: Up to NZD 5,000 toward course-related costs, covering 50% of tuition fees, compulsory student services fees and required equipment
NZD 20,000 living stipend, regardless of living situation or location of study
coverage: Up to NZD 5,000 toward course-related costs, covering 50% of tuition fees, compulsory student services fees and required equipment
NZD 20,000 living stipend, regardless of living situation or location of study
requirements: Must pass all first semester courses to receive second semester funding
Must submit a satisfactory report and an academic transcript at the end of each semester
Must reapply each year to be considered for further funding
Must take up the scholarship in the year it is offered
Must apply through Universities New Zealand using the Community Force platform
documents: Completed application form on the Universities New Zealand Community Force platform
Documents uploaded through the Community Force platform as specified in the application guidance
existing.english_requirement: Not stated as a separate requirement on the awarding body's page; study is in New Zealand, so English ability is implied by enrolment in a New Zealand qualification.
application_method: Apply online through Universities New Zealand once applications open
Complete the application form and upload the required documents on the Universities New Zealand Community Force platform
Optional: attend an information webinar, which the programme ran in June and September 2026
existing.selection_notes: The selection committee assesses each application on the impact of the scholar on refugee health outcomes, the impact of the scholar on the refugee health workforce, the impact of the scholarship on the scholar, and the likelihood of successfully attaining the qualification. Immigration New Zealand notes the programme particularly values scholars with cultural knowledge and indigenous language skills.
existing.best_fit: Former refugees and their children who resettled in New Zealand, have already begun a health-related qualification there, and intend to work in the New Zealand health workforce.
existing.notes: The total annual fund is NZD 400,000 supporting up to 16 recipients each year, as announced by Immigration New Zealand in September 2025. Because the award covers only 50% of course-related costs, it does not pay full tuition. Universities New Zealand and university pages additionally state a Level 7 minimum, NZQA-accredited provider, at least one year of completed tertiary study, and a New Zealand citizenship, permanent residency or resident visa test, and describe a mentoring programme alongside the award; those conditions are not on the Immigration New Zealand page and were not verified here, so treat them as unconfirmed until you read the Universities New Zealand regulations.
existing.duration: One academic year; recipients must reapply each year
existing.application_period: The 2027 intake opened 1 July 2026 and closed 1 October 2026. The first intake opened 15 October 2025. The programme is described as multi-year and annual, so the next window is expected to open in July 2027, but no 2028 closing date is published.
existing.program_type: Government scholarship (refugees and displaced students, health workforce)
